elements.name: 물
elements.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: production 2D hand-painted game DESTRUCTION ANIMATION SPRITE SHEET, not a poster. Input image 1 is the exact original object to preserve in frame 0 and in the surviving material of every frame. Input image 2 is the approved five elemental orbs, left to right water fire wind earth lightning; use ONLY the corresponding round orb as the released item. Generate exactly EIGHT chronological frames in a mathematically regular 4-column by 2-row grid on transparent alpha background. Equal cells, uniform widths/heights, reading order left to right top row then left to right bottom row. Canvas landscape aspect 2:1, ideally 2048x1024 so cells are 512 square. Each frame is a separate isolated sprite contained inside its cell, with 12% padding around it. Fixed camera, fixed object scale and same bottom-center ground anchor in EVERY cell. Reference object's full healthy height occupies about 70% cell height. Do not enlarge damaged states or final orb to fill cell: orb diameter is only 35% of original intact object height, remaining in the same coordinate system. Preserve hand-painted illustration style, colors, materials, lighting and proportions from reference 1. Do not add characters, weapons, impact stars, arrows, panel borders, backgrounds, ground planes, shadows, labels, numbers or text. Show actual cumulative damage, not generic squash/fade. Last cell is ONE single fully released orb floating at a consistent small height. Frame sequence: Blue ceramic water jar with cream rim and two handles. 0 intact identical jar full of water, 1 thin hairline crack on front, 2 two branching cracks and a few blue chips, 3 a missing section of rim and leaking droplets with wider cracks, 4 jar collapsing into separated large ceramic pieces with a cyan orb beginning to show, 5 low pile of ceramic shards with the same cyan orb rising clearly above, 6 cyan orb fully released above fewer shards, 7 only the cyan-blue spherical orb containing a droplet core, no jar left. Damage MUST be cumulative and materially visible at every step. Water splashes only during breakup.
